overview: Independent Ghana became a republic in 1960. Its modern history includes interrupted parliamentary government, new infrastructure, inventive crafts and public-health projects.

periods.title: Independence and the first republic
periods.summary: Independence in 1957 was followed by republican government in 1960 and a military coup in 1966.

periods.title: Alternating civilian and military governments
periods.summary: Several constitutional governments and military regimes followed one another.

sections.title: A republic and a transformed river

items.text: The map begins in 1960, when Ghana became a republic, three years after independence from Britain. Independence and the establishment of a republic were separate milestones in the country’s political history.

Ten women entered the National Assembly in 1960 through a temporary measure intended to bring women into parliamentary life. Representation is part of everyday history too: who can speak in the chamber affects whose concerns reach government.

Article 1 of the 1992 constitution begins: “The Sovereignty of Ghana resides in the people of Ghana”. This is an attested English writing sample. In plainer English, governing authority belongs to the people; it is a constitutional principle, not a claim that political life always matches it.

The Akosombo hydroelectric project was constructed from 1961 to 1965. Its dam turned the Volta’s moving water into electricity through turbines and generators. The project created a huge engineered landscape, connecting river management with factories, homes and national development.

The new reservoir also displaced communities. InOctober 1964,2,063 residents of Worobong moved to Amate, together with settlers from other villages. Historian Stephan Miescher follows these households as well as the dam: producing electricity could mean losing one’s old home and fields.

sections.title: Cloth and carpentry that carry stories

items.text: Kente makers weave narrow strips on horizontal looms and join them into cloth. Silk, cotton and rayon offer different possibilities. Patterns receive names drawn from sayings and social situations, so a carefully chosen cloth can communicate more than a favorite color.

Kente skills travel through families, apprenticeships and schools. A community’s chief weaver can settle disputes, maintain production standards and connect makers with trading networks. Learning to weave therefore involves people and institutions as well as nimble fingers.

Paa Joe’s red-pepper coffin, made around 1992, uses painted wooden planks to honor work such as growing or selling peppers. Ga workshops around Teshi and Nungua developed these striking forms. The museum stresses that specialty coffins are exceptions; most funerals use simpler rectangular ones.

Samuel Narh Nartey made a Nokia-phone-shaped coffin in 2007 for an exhibition. Its painted screen says “Hello”. He had trained for eleven years with Paa Joe. This museum commission shows skilled carpentry responding to new technology, rather than evidence that every phone owner wanted the same funeral.

A 2021 UNICEF report describes new changing rooms and urinals for schoolgirls in northern Ghana. Privacy, cleanliness and somewhere to manage menstruation made attending lessons more comfortable. A school’s essential equipment includes facilities that rarely appear in the class photograph.

Completed in 2020, the programme built 101 urinals with changing rooms across four districts, reaching more than 10,000 schoolgirls. These local improvements made attending school more comfortable. Plumbing and private space can make an educational difference alongside books and teachers.

At Ghana’s malaria-vaccine pilot launch on 30 April 2019, six-month-old Susana and Abigail received the first vaccinations in the programme. Ghana joined Kenya and Malawi in testing routine delivery. Parents, nurses and researchers all contributed to learning how a new health tool could work outside a laboratory.

ending.text: Ghana continues as an independent state. Coups ended particular governments, while constitutional rule resumed in 1993. Political changes did not end its communities or their creative work.
